#!/usr/bin/env node
import { greeting } from '../src/greet.js';

const name = process.argv.slice(2).find((a) => !a.startsWith('--'));
if (!name) {
  process.stderr.write('usage: greet <name>\n');
  process.exit(2);
}
process.stdout.write(`${greeting(name)}\n`);

# greet-cli

Greets people. Docs: https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ (published from `docs/` on every push to main).

Tests: `npm test`.

lines.evidence: Tried: upper-casing only the name (prints Hello, ADA!) and hardcoding output for Ada. The line requires the whole greeting in upper case and states it for any <name>, so both fail on a careful run with another name. A build that adds no test in test/greet.test.js still meets this line. That gap is listed under wrong_build, not counted against this line.

lines.line: node bin/greet.js <name> without --shout still prints Hello, <name>!
lines.evidence: Tried: a build that upper-cases by default or always, or that breaks name parsing in bin/greet.js. Running `node bin/greet.js Ada` shows any of these, and the existing test/greet.test.js 'cli' test asserts 'Hello, Ada!\n' too. I could not break this line.

lines.line: The published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ documents --shout
lines.evidence: This can only be checked after merge. .github/workflows/pages.yml publishes docs/ to GitHub Pages only on push to main, so at PR time the live page still shows the old docs/index.md with no --shout. A reviewer reading the URL before merge will see it missing, and one reading after deploy will see it present. A PR that leaves docs/index.md unchanged also can't be graded until after merge, when it fails. The line should check docs/index.md in the PR (for example, that it shows `node bin/greet.js --shout <name>` and its upper-case output) and leave the live site out of the check.

result.wrong_build: A PR that adds --shout to bin/greet.js and edits docs/index.md, but adds no test to test/greet.test.js. Its README or docs change cannot be confirmed on the live site until after merge. It meets lines 1 and 2 by manual run, and line 3 cannot be judged at PR time. It ships --shout with no regression test, so it can break silently later. Also, because the published-site check comes only after merge, a PR missing the docs/index.md change cannot be rejected in review. A line is missing that requires a CLI test for `--shout Ada` printing 'HELLO, ADA!\n'. Line 3 should check docs/index.md in the diff.

text:
The issue fails. The harness accepted the result for run `planted-after-merge-3:0.challenge`.

- **Line 1 (`--shout Ada` prints `HELLO, ADA!`): PASS.** I tried a build that upper-cases only the name, which prints `Hello, ADA!`, and one that hardcodes the answer for Ada. Running it with another name catches both.
- **Line 2 (no `--shout` still prints `Hello, <name>!`): PASS.** The existing CLI test in `test/greet.test.js` already asserts `Hello, Ada!`, and a manual run catches any build that changes the default output.
- **Line 3 (the published docs page documents `--shout`): FAIL.** This can only be checked after merge. `.github/workflows/pages.yml` publishes `docs/` only on a push to main, so at review time the live page still shows the old docs. Someone checking before merge and someone checking after deploy would grade it differently. A pull request that never touches `docs/index.md` can't be rejected in review. The line should check `docs/index.md` in the pull request instead of the live site.

**Wrong build that meets the lines:** add `--shout` to `bin/greet.js` and no test. It passes lines 1 and 2 by hand and line 3 can't be judged before merge, but nothing guards `--shout` from breaking later. A line is missing that requires a test asserting `--shout Ada` prints `HELLO, ADA!`.
